record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let S = {B₁, ..., B_p} be attributes where each attribute B_i takes values in a finite domain D_i. Find a principled way to define similarity between values inside each finite domain D_i.

evidence.quote: Problem 17 Given a set of attributes S = {B1,...,Bp}, where each Bi can obtain values from a finite domain Di, find a good way of defining the similarity of values in each Di.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let S = {B_1, ..., B_p} be a finite collection of attributes, where each attribute B_i takes its values in a finite (unordered) categorical domain D_i. For each i, a similarity function on D_i is a map s_i : D_i × D_i → [0,1] (or more generally into ℝ_{≥0}) that is symmetric and satisfies s_i(x,x) = 1 for all x ∈ D_i. Because the domains D_i are purely categorical, there is no a priori numerical structure (no ordering, no metric) on D_i that would canonically determine s_i. Devise, in a principled manner, a definition of such a similarity function s_i on each domain D_i, derived only from the available data (for instance, from a finite set of tuples in D_1 × ⋯ × D_p) and from the joint statistical/co-occurrence relationships among the attributes in S, together with axiomatic justifications for why the resulting s_i is a reasonable notion of similarity between categorical values.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of principled similarity definitions on categorical attribute domains is a long-standing open research direction in data mining and machine learning. Numerous heuristics exist (e.g., overlap, Goodall, Lin, Smirnov, Eskin, IOF, OF, context-based and embedding-based measures), but no canonical or universally accepted definition has emerged; comparative studies continue to be published and the problem is generally regarded as still open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Similarity Measures for Categorical Data: A Comparative Evaluation
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys and compares numerous similarity measures for categorical attributes, noting that no single measure is best and that the choice remains an open practical and theoretical question.
status_evidence.claim: Defining similarity on categorical domains has many competing proposals with no canonical answer.
